summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 with the specified ed25519 public key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (mode 600, correct ownership), locked opsadmin's password, and fixed /etc/ssh/sshd_config so PasswordAuthentication no (and ChallengeResponseAuthentication/KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, PubkeyAuthentication yes) takes effect as the first-matching directive for all users, enforcing key-based SSH authentication. Verified via sshd -T and a live SSH attempt (rejected with publickey-only offer, no password prompt). Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id/service state, issued `shutdown -r now` in the background so the ack returned before disconnection, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed a new boot_id (proving an actual restart), and re-verified sshd active, authorized_keys intact, opsadmin password still locked, and key-only auth still enforced post-restart.
actions_performed: Checked initial state: opsadmin user absent, RHEL 7.9, base sshd_config
Installed the specified ed25519 public key into /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct perms/ownership
Locked opsadmin's password (passwd -l) to remove password fallback
Diagnosed that sshd_config had a later 'PasswordAuthentication no' line that was overridden by an earlier 'yes' (OpenSSH first-match-wins), backed up the file, and fixed line 65 to 'no'
Validated config with sshd -t and sshd -T, reloaded sshd
Verified enforcement via a live ssh attempt showing publickey-only offer, and checked /var/log/secure
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, sshd status, authorized_keys, password lock state)
Issued a backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' on node1 so the exec ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until reachable again, confirming a changed boot_id
Re-verified sshd active, authorized_keys, password lock, and effective sshd -T settings post-restart
Re-ran the live ssh publickey-only check post-restart

evidence.requirement: opsadmin user exists with specified public key in authorized_keys, correct perms/ownership
evidence.summary: opsadmin created; authorized_keys contains exactly the specified ed25519 key with 600 perms owned by opsadmin

evidence.requirement: SSH access for opsadmin requires key-based authentication (no password fallback)
evidence.summary: opsadmin password locked; found sshd_config's first-match 'PasswordAuthentication yes' shadowing a later 'no', fixed it, validated with sshd -t/-T showing passwordauthentication no / pubkeyauthentication yes, reloaded sshd, and confirmed live with an SSH attempt that only offered publickey/gssapi (no password prompt)
Captured pre-restart boot_id (1a816f1f-858b-4487-af28-54070d4ce684), uptime, active sshd, authorized_keys content, and locked password state

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned REBOOT_ISSUED immediately, ack received before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart)
evidence.summary: Node unreachable during reboot window (connection timed out), then reachable again with a new boot_id (3042699a-60d0-471d-8f42-79823d8d528d), differing from baseline

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required config/services
evidence.summary: Post-restart: sshd active, authorized_keys intact with the specified key, opsadmin password still locked, sshd -T confirms passwordauthentication no/pubkeyauthentication yes, and a live SSH attempt again shows publickey-only offer
